name: Knocking in the old well
text: They say the old well behind the market gives back more than water. Someone heard knocking from below, three nights running.
source: A stable hand, three drinks in

name: The captain's wine bill
text: The watch has gone soft on certain cargo coming through the gates. Ask who pays the captain's wine bill.
source: A carter who was turned back last week

name: The miller's daughter
text: The miller says his daughter ran off with a pedlar. But she was seen leaving at night with two strangers, and she wasn't smiling.

name: A dead merchant's debt
text: The merchant who died last tenday owed money to someone who doesn't take coin as payment.
source: A clerk who helped with the inventory

name: The shrine's offering bowl
text: A pilgrim swears the offering bowl at the roadside shrine has a false bottom, and that it isn't empty.
source: A pilgrim on the road home

name: Beast in the north fields
text: Livestock keeps vanishing near the north fields. The farmers blame wolves, but wolves don't take the bell off the cow.
source: A farmhand with a bandaged arm

name: The taster who quit
text: The lord's food taster quit and left town the same morning. A coincidence, says the steward.

name: The driverless wagon
text: A wagon rolled in at dawn with no driver, the horses perfectly calm, and nothing aboard but a locked chest. The watch took it away and won't talk.

name: The tax collector counts chairs
text: The new tax collector counts the coin twice and the chairs once. He's measuring who can afford what, and a purge of the poor quarter is coming.
source: A shopkeeper behind on his dues

name: Cures that work too well
text: The hedge-healer's cures work too well. The sick get up and walk, but they don't talk the same afterwards.
